original_question: Let f2(n) be the maximum number of edges in a 2-connected graph on n vertices in which no two cycles have the same length. Is it true that lim_{n→∞} (f2(n) − n)/√n = 1?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.11 in Section 1 (“Erdős Problem 1”): if f2(n) is the maximum number of edges in a 2-connected graph on n vertices in which no two cycles have the same length, then lim_{n→∞}(f2(n)-n)/√n = 1. ([archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/pacm_download/168/4692-cycle.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s intended target almost exactly: it uses the correct extremal function f2(n), the 2-connectedness hypothesis, the distinct-cycle-length condition, and the exact conjectured limit value 1. This is essentially the wording of Conjecture 1.11 once f2(n) is read from the immediately preceding paragraph. ([archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/pacm_download/168/4692-cycle.pdf))
missing_details: The limit is over integer values of n tending to infinity; making this explicit improves stand-alone precision for an extremal graph function. ([archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/pacm_download/168/4692-cycle.pdf))

For full self-containment, “no two cycles have the same length” can be unpacked as: every two distinct cycles in the graph have different lengths. The paper leaves this phrasing as-is, but that is the intended meaning of the condition defining f2(n). ([archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/pacm_download/168/4692-cycle.pdf))

If one wants the question to be fully stand-alone outside the paper, it helps to state the optimization domain explicitly as all 2-connected n-vertex graphs G with |V(G)|=n; the paper gives this definition immediately before Theorem 1.7. ([archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/pacm_download/168/4692-cycle.pdf))

No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency data are relevant here; this is a purely graph-theoretic asymptotic extremal problem, as is implicit from Section 1’s setup of f2(n). ([archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/pacm_download/168/4692-cycle.pdf))
refined_question: For each integer n≥3, let f2(n) be the maximum number of edges of a 2-connected graph G with |V(G)|=n such that any two distinct cycles of G have different lengths. Is it true that the limit exists and satisfies lim_{n→∞}(f2(n)-n)/√n = 1? ([archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/pacm_download/168/4692-cycle.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting the paper’s exact 2-connected distinct-cycle-length conjecture, namely Conjecture 1.11, rather than the earlier conjectures about f(n) for arbitrary graphs. The only substantive refinements needed are to make the quantification over n and the pairwise-distinct-cycle-length condition fully explicit. The nearby context on page 2 gives the definition of f2(n), then records upper and lower asymptotic bounds in Theorems 1.7–1.9 and Corollary 1.10 before stating Conjecture 1.11. ([archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/pacm_download/168/4692-cycle.pdf))
